**Tesla – a whirlwind of financial strain, bold product teasers, and merger speculation**  

- **Q3 earnings shock:** Tesla’s third‑quarter profit fell 43% and automotive revenue slipped 3% while Energy Generation & Storage dropped 16%【3†L1-L1】【4†L1-L1】.  
- **Merger chatter:** Multiple outlets report that SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a merger that would require Elon Musk’s personal approval, with investors treating the two stocks as a combined bet and analysts debating the obstacles【7†L1-L1】【9†L1-L1】【10†L1-L1】【11†L1-L1】.  
- **Flying Roadster hype:** Musk unveiled a “flying” version of the Roadster, claiming production will start in 2028, but prediction‑market traders remain skeptical after years of delays【2†L1-L1】【15†L1-L1】【16†L1-L1】【17†L1-L1】.  
- **Cybertruck cancellation:** Tesla announced it will not launch the Cybertruck in Australia or New Zealand, cancelling regional production plans【1†L1-L1】.  
- **Regulatory pressure:** A NHTSA petition alleges Tesla robotaxis are exceeding speed limits in school zones, raising safety concerns【18†L1-L1】.  
- **Brand shift:** In Europe the company rebranded its Full Self‑Driving system as “Tesla Assisted Driving”【19†L1-L1】.  
- **Political spending:** Musk has poured $366 million into election campaigns, betting the Senate outcome will affect future regulation of both Tesla and SpaceX【5†L1-L1】.  

*These items capture the biggest headlines from the past two weeks, with the financial results and merger talks taking precedence over the newer product teasers and regulatory moves.*
